cards.text: Friend, the kingdom just split: Israel made Jeroboam son of Nebat king (1 Kings 12:2, 19-20), and Rehoboam, Solomon's son, rules Judah (1 Kings 11:43; 12:17). Jeroboam builds up Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, moves in, then heads out and builds Penuel too. I spent YEARS in one junk drawer, and this man is out here collecting cities like cookie boxes.

cards.question: New king, new cities. But Jeroboam has a worry he only says in his heart. What does he think might happen to his kingdom?

answers.text: It might go back to the house of David
It might be taken over by Egypt
It might be split among his sons

cards.text: Jeroboam plays out the whole worst case in his heart, the way I used to lie awake in that drawer sure every rattle meant the trash can. The house of the LORD is in Jerusalem, and that's where the people go up to offer sacrifices.

cards.question: Jeroboam says if the people go up to sacrifice in Jerusalem, their ___ will return to Rehoboam king of Judah.
True or false: Jeroboam thinks the people might kill him and go back to Rehoboam.

cards.text: So after seeking advice, the king comes up with a fix, and he makes two of something. Friend, when a fix comes in a matching set, I start sweating through my apron.

cards.question: What does Jeroboam make after seeking advice?

cards.text: Then Jeroboam tells the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you.” Friend, you tell ME something's too far and I'm sold, because I once went years without leaving a drawer.

cards.question: What does Jeroboam tell the people the golden calves are?

answers.text: The gods who brought them out of Egypt
Signs that the LORD chose Jeroboam
Guards to keep the land of Israel safe

cards.question: Jeroboam sets one golden calf up in ___ and the other in ___.

cards.text: The Bible puts it plainly: “this thing became a sin”. Jerusalem was too much, but now the people walk as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves, which is like calling in sick and then driving four hours to wait in line at a theme park.
Jeroboam isn't done. He builds shrines on the high places, and now he's got job openings, friend, because shrines need priests.

cards.question: Who does Jeroboam appoint as priests for his shrines?

answers.text: People from every class who aren't Levites
Only Levites who came up from Judah
Only elders who once served Solomon

cards.text: Next up, a feast, and you KNOW this baker perks up at the word feast. Jeroboam ordains one on the fifteenth day of the eighth month.

cards.question: True or false: Jeroboam's feast is like the feast that was in Judah.
At his feast, Jeroboam makes his offering in ___ to sacrifice to the calves he set up.
True or false: The month of Jeroboam's feast is a month God chose.

cards.text: So there he is in Bethel, offering sacrifices and burning incense at a feast he ordained for the Israelites, in a month he picked all by himself. Hang on, friend, because this story is FAR from over.

findings.problem: The joke blends two images: the junk drawer (staying in one place) and cookie boxes (collecting). The comparison's action doesn't match the fact either. Jeroboam builds cities, but 'collecting cities like cookie boxes' isn't something Papa Dorin does. He fills cookie boxes, he doesn't collect them.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: "When a fix comes in a matching set, I start sweating through my apron" doesn't click. There's no everyday experience where a matching set signals trouble, so a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The core action is being told a trip is too far. The comparison, going years without leaving a drawer, wasn't something Papa Dorin chose, so 'I'm sold' doesn't follow from it. It also nearly repeats card 1's drawer contrast.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Jerusalem was too much" states Jeroboam's claim from 12:28 as fact. The 'calling in sick and then driving four hours' comparison also connects 12:28 and 12:30, saying the trip to Dan was a bigger trip than Jerusalem. The text puts the two side by side but never makes that connection or compares the distances.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin calls himself "this baker." The docs use "baker" for the user, and papa-dorin.md says he calls the baker "baker." Using the same word for himself could confuse who he means.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin call himself a "baker," or should that word be kept only for the user?
